📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

A Level Curve Core Definition

A Level Curve a set, and indeed some level curves of some functions are notʺ curvesʺ at all.

Co-Ordinate Geometry Key Concept

Co-ordinate Geometry is an approach to investigating and solving problems in the domain of geometric objects such as straight lines, triangles, planes, cubes, etc.

Cartesian Co-Ordinate System Key Concept

In the rest of the discussion in the unit, unless mentioned otherwise, the term ' co-ordinate system' will be used for cartesian co-ordinate system, which is also called rectilinear co-ordinate system.

Graphing Linear Functions Key Concept

A function y =f(x), is called linear if the power of x in f(x) is not more than 1.

Absolute Value Function Key Concept

Absolute Value Function is given as f(x) = | x | indicating that we need to consider modulus | x | of a real number keeping it as the non-negative value without regard to its sign.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

4.2 Vertical Line Test of Function

  • 4.2: Graph that does not Represent a Function Thus, using vertical-line text we can identify the graphs that are not functions.
  • For example, you can show that each of the following graphs is not a function.
  • Thus, some of the important equations such as ellipse, circle and parabola may not represent a function.
  • It cannot be used to test (or confirm) whether a relationship is functional.

4.2.1 Relationship between Equation and Function

  • Before we discuss functions in detail, we need to be clear about the possible relationship between an equation and a relation/function.
  • Consider the equation X2+Y2=4 ………… (1) Then to talk about mathematical relation/function, we rewrite the above equation so that one of the variables, say Y is written on L.H.S.
  • (2) Next step to talk about a relation/ function corresponding to Equation (1) is to rewrite (2), so that only Y (and not its power, or square-root etc.) is written on L.H.S.
  • to a single variable, with the power of the variable as exactly 1, we can talk of a (mathematical) relation/function.

4.2.2 Co-ordinate Geometry

  • Co-ordinate Geometry is an approach to investigating and solving problems in the domain of geometric objects such as straight lines, triangles, planes, cubes, etc.
  • The approach consists in representing geometric objects as Algebraic expressions and equations like a x + b y + c =0 for a straight line, and x2+ y2= c for a circle etc.
  • And then use algebraic tools for making inferences and solving problems.
  • The process of translating geometric objects to algebraic expressions are achieved using co-ordinate systems.

4.2.3 Cartesian Co-ordinate System

  • In the rest of the discussion in the unit, unless mentioned otherwise, the term ' co-ordinate system' will be used for cartesian co-ordinate system, which is also called rectilinear co-ordinate system.
  • 4.6 below, form the basis of rectangular co-ordinate system for 2-dimension 1) The horizontal number line is called the x- axis.
  • 2) The vertical number line is called the y-axis.
  • The origin is where the two lines/axes intersect.

4.3 Translating Geometric Figures to Algebraic Equations

  • 4.7, let us take P (x, y) outside the segment A (0, -2)and B (2, 0), and drop a perpendicular PQ on x-axis.
  • From conventional/synthetic geometry, we know: IAOI / IAQI = IBOI / IPQI, ...
  • (i) Where, IXI denotes length of line segment X.
  • 4.11 : Hyperbola : (x)2 - (y)2 = 1 • xy=c2 for Rectangular Hyperbola.

4.4 Graphing Linear Functions

  • A function y =f(x), is called linear if the power of x in f(x) is not more than 1.
  • A linear function corresponds to a linear equation A x + B y + C = 0, in which degrees of x and y do not exceed 1, and A, B, C are constants.
  • To plot a graph of a function, we take, one by one, values in the domain (xi) as the independent variable x, and then find the corresponding values in the range yi of the dependent variable y.
  • It helps record the x and y values while plotting the graphs.

4.4.1 Absolute Value Function

  • Absolute Value Function is given as f(x) = | x | indicating that we need to consider modulus | x | of a real number keeping it as the non-negative value without regard to its sign.
  • That is, |x| = x for a positive x, |x| = -x for a negative x (in which case –x is positive), and |0| = 0.
  • Example: ƒ is a function given by f (x) = |x| + 2.
  • The y interceptis given by (0, ƒ(0)) = (0, |-2|) =(0, 2); x intercept is at the point (2,0)since we solve for |x-2| =0.But 0 =y=f(x)= |x-2|=0 has no solution.

4.4.2 Step Function

  • A step function (or staircase function) is a piecewise function containing all constant “pieces” .
  • The constant pieces are observed across the adjacent intervals of the function, as they change value from one interval to the next.
  • You cannot draw a step function without removing your pencil from your paper.
  • Example of a step function: For definition of our particular step function y=f(x), First, we write every x = Int - x + Fraction-x, where Fraction-x>0.
